Grade is a market, not a label

A graded card trades on its grade, and the steps between grades are not evenly spaced. On a card with real demand the gap between a 9 and a 10 can be several multiples, while lower grades compress together.

Card AI prices graded cards by grade rather than applying a flat premium to a raw price, so the number reflects the market that copy actually sits in.

Raw and slabbed copies of the same card, side by side

  • Raw cards are recorded with their condition
  • Graded cards are recorded with the grading company and grade, covering PSA, BGS, CGC and SGC
  • Both can exist in your collection at once, for the same card, each valued on its own market
  • That makes the raw versus graded spread visible instead of theoretical

What this does not do

Card AI tracks the grade you record from the slab. It does not predict what a raw card would grade if you submitted it, and it does not measure centering from a photograph. Those are estimates, and estimates are not what the market pays.

Graded card tracker questions.

Can I use Card AI as a PSA card value tracker?

Yes, for cards that are already graded. Record PSA as the grading company and enter the grade printed on the slab to see available grade-specific values. Card AI does not connect to PSA or predict the grade of a raw card.

Which grading companies are supported?

Graded cards are recorded with the grading company and grade, covering PSA, BGS, CGC and SGC.

Can I hold the same card both raw and graded?

Yes. They are stored as separate entries with separate values, which is what lets you compare the raw and graded price of the same card.

Will Card AI tell me what grade my raw card would get?

No. You record the grade from the slab for cards that are already graded. Card AI does not predict grades or measure centering from a photograph.
